subject: Planned IO firmware sweep and rolling node drains — us-west-3 (low-impact window)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Ruiz <olivia@acmecloud.com>, platform-ops@acmecloud.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Planned IO firmware sweep and rolling node drains — us-west-3

Hi Olivia / Acme platform team,

Quick heads-up: we’re scheduling a targeted IO firmware sweep in the us-west-3 region that requires rolling node drains. We’ve scoped this as a low-impact maintenance window but wanted to share details and recommended actions in case you want to take any pre-emptive steps.

Window (planned):
- UTC: Aug 11, 2026 02:00 – 05:00 UTC
- Local: evening US Pacific (night maintenance)

What we’ll do:
- Sequentially drain and reboot a small percentage of inference nodes for NVMe controller firmware updates and a microcode hotfix.
- Nodes will be drained gracefully; active KV caches will be preserved where possible and requests will be routed to healthy replicas.
- We’ll run small-scale verification (end-to-end sampling) after each drain before returning capacity to service.

Expected impact:
- Brief routing of a small fraction of requests (<1.5% measured historically) to warm fallback nodes for <30s per affected request.
- No model restarts are expected; in-flight requests will be retried by our gateway when safe.

What we recommend you do (optional):
1) Pin critical production routes to a fallback model variant (if you use multiple variants) for the window.
2) If you have latency-sensitive SLAs for specific tokens/requests, schedule non-critical batches outside the window.
3) Share a contact for on-call escalation (reply with name/phone/email).

Attachments: maintenance brief and calendar invite attached.

We’ll post real-time status to the region maintenance doc and provide a short post-maintenance summary within 24 hours. If you prefer we move the window, let us know by EOD Aug 10.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of NetOps 
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Ruiz <olivia@acmecloud.com>

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned IO firmware sweep and rolling node drains — us-west-3

Thanks Neha — appreciate the notice. A couple quick questions: 

1) Will this affect dedicated capacity pools under our Dedicated contract? We have a small reserved pool in us-west-3.
2) What are your rollback criteria if we see degraded tail latency beyond our SLA?

We’d prefer minimal change to our routing during the work; if there’s a short window where we see higher error rates, please callback to platform-ops@acmecloud.com and loop in Raj.

—Olivia
Olivia Ruiz
Platform Reliability Lead, Acme Cloud

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned IO firmware sweep and rolling node drains — us-west-3

Hi Olivia — quick answers and mitigations below.

1) Dedicated pools: We will not touch customer-dedicated tenant hosts unless explicitly scheduled with you. Your reserved pool is isolated; standard rolling actions will target the shared host layer only. If you have pinned hosts in the dedicated pool, they will remain untouched.

2) Rollback criteria & mitigations:
- If we observe sustained p95/p99 latency degradation beyond 20% of baseline for three consecutive 5-minute windows, we’ll automatically abort further drains and begin an immediate rollback to prior NVMe firmware with priority scheduling.
- We’ll enable aggressive request hedging to fallback nodes for the period and increase sampling on tail latency.
- On the operations side, we’ll pause drains for the next batch and escalate to the on-call systems team.

Operational contacts: Ben Carter (on-call infra lead) +1 415 555 0198 (work); Sean Gallagher (SRE) is available for live triage.

We’ll also publish a short playbook in the shared drive during the work so your team can correlate our node IDs with your routing metrics.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Ruiz <olivia@acmecloud.com>, platform-ops@acmecloud.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-maintenance summary — us-west-3 IO firmware sweep (Aug 11)

Hi Olivia / Acme ops,

Thanks again for the coordination. A brief post-maintenance summary and next steps:

What we did:
- Performed rolling drains on 12 node groups across us-west-3 between 02:05–04:42 UTC on Aug 11.
- Applied NVMe controller firmware and a microcode hotfix; each node was validated with a smoke pass before rejoining.

Observed impact:
- Measured request routing increased transiently for ~1.1% of requests; median additional latency for affected requests was ~18s due to retries, but 99th percentile was within expected bounds.
- No Dedicated pool hosts were modified (confirmed with the dedicated tenancy flag).

Postmortem & artifacts:
- Draft postmortem uploaded: https://drive.google.com/fakeid/usw3-postmortem (attachment: postmortem-draft.docx)
- Maintenance brief and verification logs: https://docs.redwood.ai/maintenance/us-west-3

Actions taken:
- Enabled short-term hedging on high-priority routes for 48h to reduce retry tail exposure.
- Created a follow-up task to add earlier signaling from our gateway when we detect NVMe-induced retries.

If you saw anything unexpected on your side, please reply-all with screenshots/metrics; we’ll add it to the postmortem and follow up. We’ll finalize the postmortem in 72 hours and share final RCA.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of NetOps
Redwood Inference
